Quick question as we prepare for our SOC 2 readiness review: we need to remove a small set of debug traces generated during a tenant-scoped incident (tenant id: ST-8732) and provide proof that the deletion occurred. We are on a tight timeline — the compliance window is next Friday — so any concrete steps you can share are appreciated.

Thanks,
Megan Turner
Director, Information Security
Soteria Health

Hi Megan — thanks for the note and the heads-up on the timeline. Short answers up front: yes (we support targeted tenant log deletion for private and dedicated customers), typical ETA depends on scope but we can commit to a discrete workflow for your ST-8732 shard, and proof-of-delete can include export certificates + deletion runbook logs and a signed attestation from Redwood Security.

Looping in Kimberly (Security) and Priya (Legal) to propose the exact evidence bundle and run the deletion with the right controls. Kimberly — can you confirm the technical steps and whether we need a scoped Legal signoff prior to execution?

Ben

ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Megan Turner <megan.turner@soteriahealth.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Targeted log deletion / proof-of-delete process

Megan / Ben — thanks. Below is the proposed technical workflow (we will follow this exactly and produce the attached artifacts):

1) Scope confirmation (same-day): identify exact log shards / indices that map to tenant ST-8732. Customer to confirm list (or we will provide an initial query snapshot).

2) Export & snapshot (T+0): create a read-only encrypted snapshot of the identified shards and store it in a customer-specific, access-controlled bucket for 7 days (for audit only). Snapshot manifest will include file-level SHA256 checksums.

3) Deletion (T+1): run the targeted erase job on the runtime nodes (we support per-tenant index-level deletion in Dedicated and Private deployments). We will record the deletion job id, node ids, and exact sequence numbers deleted. Deletions are executed with multi-step confirmation (dry-run, confirm, finalize) to avoid collateral data loss.

4) Post-delete verification (T+1): re-run the discovery query to confirm zero hits; produce a verification log that lists the query, timestamp, and result set count.

5) Evidence bundle (T+1 to T+2): deliver the following artifacts as a signed package:
   - Snapshot manifest (SHA256 checksums) [soteria_log-retention-evidence.pdf]
   - Deletion job record with job id and node traces [redwood-deletion-process-diagram.png — process map, and internal job logs extract]
   - Signed attestation describing the procedure and who performed it (PKI-signed by Redwood Security)
   - SIG/CAIQ mapping sheet indicating which controls this action addresses [sig-caiq-mapping-20280704.xlsx]

Notes / constraints:
- For Hosted (multi-tenant) customers we can only remove customer data from application-layer indices and must follow the hosted retention policies; however, Soteria is on a Dedicated environment so full index-level removal is available.
- If the snapshot needs to be retained longer than 7 days for your internal review, we can extend retention with an audit trail (please confirm).
- Legal signoff (Priya) required if the deletion intersects data under an existing litigation hold or regulatory hold.

Megan, please confirm the exact list of indices or I can run the initial discovery query if you prefer. Once you confirm scope we will schedule T+0/T+1 windows — typical end-to-end for a small shard (under 50GB) is 24–48 hours.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Attachments: soteria_log-retention-evidence.pdf (manifest), redwood-deletion-process-diagram.png (flow), sig-caiq-mapping-20280704.xlsx (control mapping)

If you can start the discovery today, we need the evidence bundle by Friday 2028-07-06 COB.

Megan
